correctness.rationale: At any strict-sign synchronous endemic equilibrium, differentiation of the nonlinear equations gives the block Jacobian \(\begin{psmallmatrix}aI&-hI\\ I&-I-L\end{psmallmatrix}\), where \(a=bs(1-2s)\) and \(h=ks\). Orthogonal graph-Laplacian modes have \(p_\ell(z)=z^2+(1+\ell-a)z+h-a(1+\ell)\). The two-root condition gives \(h-a=-s g\prime(s)>0\) on the upper endemic branch. The quadratic Hurwitz criterion proves the sharp network threshold. For the two-community rational specialization, nonlinear sum/difference equations give the complete unequal positive both-negative-opinion branch, with \(v^2=(1-6w)(1+10w)/(324(1+2w)^2)\), and exact full-Jacobian determinant \( -81(1+2w)x_1x_2 v^2<0\). Symbolic checks passed; finite-network spectra are illustrative, not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The motivating arXiv:2608.31032v1 provides the coupled higher-order SIS--opinion model and establishes bistability only relative to its synchronous invariant set (Section IV-A, Theorem 2). It does not provide the full heterogeneous-mode threshold or the two-node nonsynchronous unstable equilibrium branch in the material inspected. General network Turing instability (Kouvaris et al 2015), higher-order contagion bistability (Iacopini et al 2019), and awareness feedback (Just et al 2017/2018) are acknowledged; the claim is limited to the explicit coupled model-specific criterion and nonlinear subcritical pitchfork.
residual_risks: Broader reaction--diffusion theorems may imply the elementary modal Routh--Hurwitz part; no novelty is claimed for that method.

value.rationale: A published epidemic--opinion model proves bistability only along synchrony, leaving the natural question whether heterogeneous outbreaks preserve it. The theorem gives a sharp necessary-and-sufficient spectral condition on any undirected opinion graph, proves that increasing protective-opinion coupling may destroy stable endemic synchrony, and identifies an exact subcritical two-patch nonlinear mechanism with unstable unequal equilibria. The result is an interpretable model-specific stability boundary and analytical benchmark, not merely an arbitrary numerical slice or a renamed general Turing formula.
